testName: Air Brakes Test #1 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: A safety valve opens at ____ pounds per square inch (psi).
questions.explanation: The safety valve protects air tanks and the air brake system by releasing air if pressure gets too high. It normally opens at 150 psi.

questions.question: An alcohol evaporator is most important:
questions.explanation: Some air brake systems have an alcohol evaporator. It adds alcohol to the system to prevent ice from forming in cold weather.

questions.question: An application pressure gauge shows:

options.text: How much air pressure is being applied to the brakes.
How much air pressure is available.
How much air pressure is needed to stop a vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: How much air pressure is being applied to the brakes.
questions.explanation: An application pressure gauge shows how much air pressure is being applied to the brakes. It helps drivers spot brake fade problems.

questions.question: Friction in an S-cam brake happens when the brake shoes and linings:

options.text: Press against the outside of the brake drum.
Press against the inside of the brake drum.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press against the inside of the brake drum.
questions.explanation: Friction happens when the brake shoes and linings press against the inside of the drum. This friction slows and stops the vehicle.

questions.question: If air pressure drops between ____, a low pressure warning should already be on.
questions.explanation: A low pressure warning should turn on before air pressure drops to between 55 and 75 psi. The warning can be a light, buzzer, or wig wag.

questions.question: Do not drive if a brake drum has a crack larger than ____ of the friction area width.
questions.explanation: Check brake drums during your walk-around inspection before driving. Do not drive if any brake drum has a crack larger than one half of the friction area width.

questions.question: How many feet does an air brake vehicle need to stop when traveling at 55 mph under ideal conditions?
questions.explanation: Total stopping distance includes perception time, reaction time, brake lag, and braking distance. An air brake vehicle at 55 mph needs about 450 feet to stop under ideal conditions.

questions.question: Why should you drain the air tanks regularly?

options.text: Because the air gets old and needs to be replaced
Because compressed air contains water that collects in the tanks
To allow for a change in pressure

questions.correctAnswerText: Because compressed air contains water that collects in the tanks
questions.explanation: Compressed air contains moisture and compressor oil that build up in the tanks and can damage the brake system. Drain tanks at the end of each driving day using the manual drain valve.

questions.question: If the safety relief valve releases air:

options.text: Something is wrong with the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Something is wrong with the brakes.
questions.explanation: The safety relief valve releases air if pressure gets too high. If it operates, something is wrong with the system and needs to be checked by a mechanic.

questions.question: A low air pressure warning should turn on when tank pressure falls below:
questions.explanation: The low air pressure warning must turn on when tank pressure falls below 60 psi. The warning can be a light, buzzer, or wig wag.

questions.question: When parked on a flat surface, you should:

options.text: Use wheel chocks to stop your vehicle from moving.
Use wheel chocks only if you have set the parking brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use wheel chocks to stop your vehicle from moving.
questions.explanation: When parking on a level surface, use wheel chocks. This is important if your vehicle does not have spring brakes. Wheel chocks prevent your trailer from rolling.

questions.question: Air brakes work using ____.
questions.explanation: Air brakes work by using compressed air.

questions.question: A wig wag is:

options.text: A device that warns when air pressure is low.
A tube that carries air to the brakes.
A type of air brake system.

questions.correctAnswerText: A device that warns when air pressure is low.
questions.explanation: A wig wag is a low air pressure warning device. It drops a mechanical arm into your view if the air pressure drops between 55 and 75 psi. Vehicles with air brakes must have this type of warning device.

questions.question: What happens if air pressure gets too low in an air brake system?
questions.explanation: If you press and release the brake pedal too many times, air leaks out faster than the compressor can replace it. When air pressure gets too low, the air brakes may stop working.

questions.question: For a single vehicle with air brakes, the leakage rate should be no more than ____ in one minute during a static leakage test.
questions.explanation: During a static leakage test on a single vehicle with air brakes, the leakage rate should be no more than 2 psi per minute. If air leaks faster than this, do not drive the vehicle. Something needs to be repaired.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT part of an air brake system?
questions.explanation: Air brake systems include an air compressor, air storage tanks, gauges, a low pressure warning device, safety valves, brake pedals, foundation brakes, spring brakes, and parking brake controls. An air filter is not part of the air brake system.

questions.question: Vehicles with Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS) have ____ warning lights to show when the ABS is not working.
questions.explanation: Vehicles with ABS have yellow warning lights. These lights alert you when the ABS is not working. Know where the warning light is on your vehicle before you drive.

questions.question: Air storage tanks:

options.text: Are not allowed on a vehicle.
Hold compressed air for the brakes.
Should be emptied of excess air after every trip.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold compressed air for the brakes.
questions.explanation: Air storage tanks hold compressed air used by the brakes. The number and size of tanks varies depending on the vehicle.

questions.question: In newer vehicles, the parking brake is applied by:

options.text: Moving a lever to the right.

questions.explanation: In newer vehicles with air brakes, the parking brake is controlled by a yellow, diamond-shaped knob. Pull the knob out to apply the parking brakes. Push it in to release them.

questions.question: What prevents the wheels from locking up when you brake?
questions.explanation: An Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) prevents the wheels from locking up when you apply the brakes.

questions.question: What does it mean if the safety relief valve in an air brake system is releasing air?

options.text: This is normal and you should not worry.
Something is wrong with the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Something is wrong with the brakes.
questions.explanation: The safety relief valve releases air to prevent the system pressure from getting too high. If it starts releasing air, something is wrong. Have a mechanic repair it.

questions.question: In a dual air brake system, what happens if one air system has very low pressure?

options.text: Either the front or rear brakes will not work fully.
There will be no noticeable problem.

questions.correctAnswerText: Either the front or rear brakes will not work fully.
questions.explanation: In a dual air brake system, either the front or rear brakes will not work fully if one air system gets too low. If air pressure gets too low while driving, pull off the road and park as soon as you can.

questions.question: What type of force do emergency brakes use?
questions.explanation: Air brakes have three separate systems: service brakes, parking brakes, and emergency brakes. Emergency and parking brakes use mechanical force.

questions.question: When you leave a vehicle unattended, what should you do?

options.text: Set the parking brake only if parked on a slope.
Let out 10 percent of the tire air.

questions.explanation: Always apply the parking brake when you leave your vehicle unattended.

questions.question: What is the ____ between an air compressor and reservoir tank that prevents air from escaping if the compressor leaks?
questions.explanation: A one-way check valve must be placed between the air compressor and the first main reservoir. It stops air from leaking out of the system if the compressor develops a leak.
